Evidence to capture: Customer, site, endpoint, device owner, workload criticality, maintenance window, and responsible technician
Why it matters: Ties evidence and authority to the correct asset before troubleshooting begins
Source or command: Asset record or approved service ticket

Evidence to capture: Windows edition, version, OS build, architecture, and last successful update date
Why it matters: Prevents comparing logs or remediation paths across unlike operating-system states
Source or command: System information and update history

Evidence to capture: Update KB, classification, release date, deployment ring, deadline, and current applicability
Why it matters: Identifies the exact update and whether the endpoint still requires it
Source or command: RMM or update-management record plus current scan

Evidence to capture: Original failure code, message, job state, attempt time, reboot state, and console screenshot or export
Why it matters: Preserves the first failure before retries or reporting refreshes change the visible state
Source or command: RMM or update-management job evidence

Evidence to capture: Collection start and end time, local time zone, clock offset, and collector identity
Why it matters: Makes event correlation defensible across the endpoint, RMM, proxy, and service desk
Source or command: System clock and collection record

Evidence to capture: Readable WindowsUpdate.log output path, generation time, file size, and cryptographic hash when retained
Why it matters: Proves which converted log was reviewed and prevents confusing it with a later regeneration
Source or command: Get-WindowsUpdateLog and approved file-hash method

Evidence to capture: Windows Update ETL source path or retained package and whether ForceFlush or IncludeAllLogs was used
Why it matters: Records how the readable log was produced and any scope-changing options
Source or command: Get-WindowsUpdateLog parameters and Microsoft documentation

Evidence to capture: WindowsUpdateClient Operational events covering the failure window
Why it matters: Provides a second event source for scan, download, install, and restart timing
Source or command: Event Viewer or approved event-log export

Evidence to capture: Earliest meaningful error in the failure sequence with 10 to 20 surrounding lines
Why it matters: Reduces the chance of treating a downstream symptom as the initiating cause
Source or command: WindowsUpdate.log review

Evidence to capture: All KB, HRESULT, Error, Failed, FATAL, warning, and phase markers relevant to the same attempt
Why it matters: Creates a bounded search trail instead of an unreviewed full-log attachment
Source or command: Approved text search or log-analysis method

Evidence to capture: Scan start, source selection, metadata result, and scan completion or failure
Why it matters: Separates detection and metadata problems from download or installation problems
Source or command: WindowsUpdate.log and update-management evidence

Evidence to capture: Download start, content source, proxy or delivery path, transfer result, and retry pattern
Why it matters: Identifies content-delivery failures before resetting update components
Source or command: WindowsUpdate.log BITS proxy and network evidence

Evidence to capture: Install start, installer or handler identity, prerequisite checks, return code, and rollback markers
Why it matters: Distinguishes applicability, prerequisite, handler, and servicing failures
Source or command: WindowsUpdate.log setup events and update history

Evidence to capture: Commit, reboot, resume, and post-reboot result with the exact boot or restart time
Why it matters: Shows whether staging succeeded but finalization or restart processing failed
Source or command: WindowsUpdate.log system events and reboot evidence

Evidence to capture: Servicing-stack, component-store, system-file, and pending-reboot findings captured before repair
Why it matters: Prevents destructive or unnecessary cache resets from erasing the diagnostic path
Source or command: Approved Microsoft diagnostics and servicing logs

Evidence to capture: Effective update source, WSUS or cloud policy, deferral, pause, deadline, ring, and conflicting manager evidence
Why it matters: Proves which authority controlled the endpoint during the failed attempt
Source or command: Policy result and update-management configuration

Evidence to capture: DNS, proxy, TLS inspection, time synchronization, required service, and content-access evidence
Why it matters: Separates local servicing failure from an unavailable or intercepted update path
Source or command: Approved network and service checks

Evidence to capture: Free disk, battery or power state, maintenance-window duration, active installer, and restart-blocker evidence
Why it matters: Surfaces environmental prerequisites that can invalidate a retry
Source or command: System and job evidence

Evidence to capture: One healthy peer with the same ring, update, build, application profile, and relevant policy
Why it matters: Finds the first point of divergence and distinguishes device-specific from shared failures
Source or command: Healthy-peer evidence with sensitive data excluded

Evidence to capture: Count and list of installed, failed, pending, offline, unknown, not-applicable, superseded, and deferred endpoints
Why it matters: Bounds customer and fleet risk instead of closing after one device succeeds
Source or command: Current cohort export or reconciled query

Evidence to capture: Approved cause statement, selected repair, authority, commands or changes, start and end time, output, and rollback path
Why it matters: Connects the evidence-led diagnosis to one bounded change
Source or command: Change or incident record

Evidence to capture: Fresh scan, installed build or update history, applicability, service health, management check-in, and representative business test
Why it matters: Proves recovery beyond a cleared error or a successful retry message
Source or command: Post-change endpoint and management evidence

Evidence to capture: Residual exposure, compensating controls, approver, owner, expiry, next retry, vendor case, and explicit closure criteria
Why it matters: Keeps unresolved patch risk visible and time bounded
Source or command: Exception register or approved risk record

Evidence to capture: Final cohort reconciliation, evidence location, customer communication, decision date, lessons, and runbook or rule changes
Why it matters: Closes every affected endpoint and converts a repeatable failure into an operational improvement
Source or command: Incident problem change or service record
